analysis.title: Q3 2026 Earnings Takes: Growth Holds In The 30s
key_insights: Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth is on track for 34% yoy, flat with Q2, against a record-high bottom-up consensus bar of 26.7% (excluding recoveries from recessions). Based on 306 companies reported (62% of market cap, 66% of earnings).

84% of companies have beaten so far, down from a record 89% in Q2 but above the 74% historical average. The aggregate beat is 4.6% (Q2: 8.6%, historical average 4.9%). Ex-Alphabet, the aggregate beat is 5.7%. The median company beat is 4.3% vs a 3.5% average.

Sales beats moderated: breadth 71% vs 59% historical, aggregate beat 2.0% vs 0.5%, median company 1.1% vs 0.6%. These are the lowest in 6 quarters but still above average. Margin beats are near average: breadth 79% vs 74%, aggregate 39bps vs 44bps, median 44bps vs 35bps.

Tech (MCG & Tech) earnings growth is 53% in Q3 (54% in Q2) and contributes 19.9pp of S&P 500 growth (19.5pp in Q2). Semis grew 145% (flat), Tech Hardware 57% to 53%, Software & Services slowed from 29% to 11%, and hyperscalers from 17% to 12%.
Energy & Materials earnings growth rose from 108% in Q2 to 119% in Q3, contributing 7.2pp (6.8pp in Q2), with oil and commodity prices elevated. Energy grew 138% to 156%.

Tech plus Energy & Materials account for 3/4 of Q3 growth. DB calls the focus on narrowness misleading: growth excluding these 3 sectors is 12.2% (13.7% in Q2), adding 7pp, one of the highest since the GFC outside the 2018 tax cuts and the post-pandemic rebound, vs an 11% long-run non-recession average.

Breadth of growth: every sector is growing at least 6% and 7 of 11 are in double digits. Median company earnings growth is 14.4% in both Q2 and Q3, the highest in 20 years outside recession recoveries. Financials slowed from 23% to 6% and Materials from 50% to 39%. Industrials (ex-Boeing) accelerated from 13% to 18%.

Sales growth is 14.4% in Q3 (14.5% in Q2). Aggregate S&P 500 margin rose from 15.8% to 16.4%, a record. MCG & Tech margin is 28.8% and Energy & Materials 14.7%, both at new highs. The rest of the index is at 11.8%, flat.

Q4 bottom-up consensus is up +0.5% since the season began, against a typical cut of -1.0%. The upgrade is entirely Energy (+16.3% on higher oil). Ex-Energy it is -0.5%, and ex-Energy and Tech it is -0.9%. MCG & Tech is -0.1%, cut last week after Alphabet's results. Consumer Cyclicals -3.6%, Utilities -3.3%, Materials -1.9%, Consumer Defensives -1.6% and Industrial Cyclicals -1.0% were cut.

Consensus expects Q4 growth of 29.4%, a record entering a season. DB forecasts 32%. Consensus has MCG & Tech at 43% (19pp contribution), Energy & Materials at 108% (6pp) and the rest of the S&P at 10% (5pp).
DB raised its S&P 500 EPS forecast for 2026 from $358 to $362 (30% yoy) and for 2027 from $420 to $430 (19%). Consensus is $359 (29%) for 2026 and $426 (19%) for 2027.

The S&P 500 is down -2.9% so far in the season, vs a typical +2% rally in the first four weeks. MCG & Tech fell -8.6% while the other 10 sectors returned 0.7% to 7.4%. DB upgraded Tech back to overweight on Oct 30, after tactically downgrading it three weeks earlier, saying the rotation out of Tech has run its course.
Post-report stock performance is positive, with the median company up in 9 of 11 sectors. Beaters have outperformed more than is typical and missers have underperformed less than in the past.

market_movers.rationale: Alphabet's Q3 earnings missed markedly, pulling the aggregate beat to 4.6% from 5.7% ex-Alphabet. Q4 estimates for MCG & Tech were cut last week after the results.

sector_views.rationale: DB upgraded Tech back to overweight on Oct 30 after tactically cutting it to neutral three weeks earlier. The rotation out of Tech is seen as having run its course and risk-reward looks favorable after the correction. Tech earnings growth is 53%.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 aggregate earnings growth tracking 34% yoy on DB's adjusted basis (Q2: 34%). Companies reported so far grew 31%, and 34% assumes the remaining companies beat at the current ex-Alphabet rate. Consensus entering the season was 26.7%. DB's numbers adjust for one-time items.
Q3 aggregate EPS beat of 4.6% (reported so far, DB adjusted) vs 8.6% in Q2 and a 4.9% average. Ex-Alphabet it is 5.7%. 84% of companies beat, vs 89% in Q2 and 74% on average.
Q4 2026 earnings growth: consensus estimate 29.4% (a forecast), DB forecast 32%.
S&P 500 EPS forecasts: DB 2026 $362 (raised from $358), 2027 $430 (raised from $420). Consensus estimates are $359 for 2026 and $426 for 2027. All are forecasts.

Q3 2026 base-quarter adjustments: Alphabet -$8.4bn securities gains, Uber -$4.9bn one-time tax benefit, Meta +$15.5bn one-time tax expense. Q3 2026 adjustments: Alphabet +$7.0bn losses, Meta +$7.8bn litigation settlements, Eli Lilly +$3.4bn acquired IP R&D charge.

Sector Q3 earnings growth (reported so far, Q2 to Q3): Energy 138% to 156%, Industrials 13% to 18%, Utilities 13% to 15%, Telecom 9% to 13%, Health Care 8% to 12%, Consumer Cyclicals 8% to 9%, Financials 23% to 6%, Materials 50% to 39%, Consumer Defensives 10% to 7%, Real Estate 9% to 6%.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US Technology sector (upgraded back from neutral on Oct 30 2026)
trade_ideas.rationale: The sharp correction improves risk-reward and the rotation out of Tech has run its course.

risk_factors: Narrow earnings growth: Tech and Energy & Materials account for 3/4 of Q3 growth (DB argues the ex-those-sectors rate of 12.2% is still robust).
Alphabet's marked earnings miss and the resulting Q4 estimate cuts for MCG & Tech.
Q4 estimate upgrades rely entirely on Energy and higher oil prices, with other sectors cut.
Slowing growth in Software & Services (29% to 11%) and hyperscalers (17% to 12%).
Beats and margins are normalizing from very high levels, and the sales beat breadth is at a 6-quarter low.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth excluding Tech and Energy & Materials is 12.2%, among the highest since the GFC. The median company is growing in the mid-teens (14.4%), every sector is at 6% or better, and 7 of 11 sectors are in double digits.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech and Energy & Materials account for 3/4 of Q3 growth, and Q4 estimate upgrades come entirely from Energy. Ex-Energy and Tech, Q4 estimates are down 0.9%.
